# An image cut into words

A transformer has no idea what a picture is. It reads a **sequence**. So the entire trick of
the Vision Transformer is the first node: turn a 32×32 image into 64 tokens, then run the
same machinery that reads text.

**The patch embedding is a plain `Conv2d`.** Kernel 4, stride 4, no padding — a convolution
whose window never overlaps, so each output position is one 4×4 patch turned into a vector of
128 numbers. That is *all* "an image is worth 16×16 words" means, and here it is one node
with two widgets set equal to each other.

After that: `flatten` the two spatial axes together, `transpose` so the 64 patches become the
time axis, add learned positions because attention has no inherent order, and from there it
is a text model.

## The result, which is not the one the architecture's fame suggests

| model | parameters | validation |
|---|---|---|
| ViT, 4 blocks, width 128 | 545,930 | 0.4390 |
| ViT, 3 blocks, width 64 | 108,426 | 0.4415 |
| **plain CNN, 3 conv blocks** | **94,762** | **0.5415** |

**The convolutional network wins by 0.10**, with a fifth of the parameters. That gap is many
times the seed spread; it is not noise.

And look at the two ViT rows. Five times the parameters changed nothing — 0.439 against
0.4415. **It is not running out of capacity.** It is running out of data.

A convolution has two assumptions built into its wiring: nearby pixels are related, and a
feature is the same feature wherever it appears. It gets those for free. Attention assumes
nothing and connects every patch to every other, so it has to *learn* that structure from
examples — and on 6,000 images there are not enough examples to learn it from.

This is the actual finding of the ViT paper, which needed on the order of a hundred million
images before transformers overtook convolutions. The architecture is not better. It is
better **given enough data**, and this workflow is a demonstration of the other side of that
sentence.

## Two Trainers, on purpose

The transformer trains at learning rate 0.001 and the convolutional net at 0.002, because
that is roughly where each is happiest. Handing both the same number would make one of them
look bad for a reason that has nothing to do with architecture.

It is worth saying out loud, because "we used identical settings" sounds fairer than it is —
identical settings are only fair when the two things want the same settings.
